clue.text: Genus like the heaths? Positive Erica's involved here

indicators.note: things that are involved are tangled up together, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for positive
taken as written, the possessive S included

explanation.surface: A botanist muses that an upbeat plant called Erica is part of a heath-like genus.
explanation.walkthrough: Erica is the botanical name of heather, which makes the surface feel like a straight definition; here it is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Epacris is an Australasian plant genus of heath-like shrubs, often called the Australian heaths.

clue.text: Alice I depict reframed for show

clue.text: Commend higher bid under pressure

explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone is to commend them, a straightforward synonym for expressing approval.

clue.text: Veto following revolutionary measure in Athens

clue.text: Sweet dance held up by northern ball

clue.text: Lad holding a game up: The Lord of the Rings

clue.text: Animal membranes — name is Attic, primarily

clue.text: Shift in Pacific? Reported low more than once

clue.text: High-flown Latin in translation

clue.text: Token person busy during Henry's dissolution?

explanation.definitionFit: Abbey counters were brass reckoning tokens used in monastic accounting, so the phrase names a kind of token as well as a monastery tallier.

clue.text: Concerning smell in lavatory bowl before we arrived?

clue.text: Gods introducing a new goddess

taken as written

clue.text: Lovemaking rarely working under a rug? Yes
